source_review.notes: Checked current Linux tracing, ftrace, tracepoint, kprobe, eBPF verifier, syscall, map, ring-buffer, BTF and libbpf documentation plus the current Linux perf_event_open man page. All eleven official URLs returned HTTP 200 after normal redirects. Hook semantics, verifier admission, CO-RE portability, transport behavior, operational guidance and inference limits remain separately scoped.

evidence: Checked source, run, filtered, map-update, emitted, delivered and decoded event-count notation and stage ordering.
Reviewed transport and decode loss, delivery fraction, Bernoulli sampling expectation and inverse-probability estimator.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation distinguishes populations and denominators across the observation pipeline and explicitly suspends monotone-count assumptions under aggregation or fan-out.

evidence: Recomputed 19,950/20,000 as 99.75 percent update success, 1,200/1,250 as 96 percent transport delivery and 1,188/1,200 as 99 percent decode success.
Confirmed 1,188/100,000 as 1.188 percent and 1,250 minus 1,188 as 62 known post-emission losses.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The deterministic computation validates five ratios/differences only; it does not establish source completeness, unbiased sampling, event semantics or causal inference.

evidence: Re-derived monotone one-to-one pipeline counts and identified aggregation and fan-out as explicit counterexamples.
Verified transport and decode loss definitions and inverse-probability count estimation only under a fixed population with independent Bernoulli inclusion.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Adaptive filters, periodic sampling, scheduling, burst loss, multiplicity and missing source counts remain outside the simplified estimator.
